result.summary:
This direction is only partly done. The literature synthesis is posted as finding f-003 and rests on the abstracts and introductions of five full texts. These are saved under /Users/nramachandra/hep-genesis-testing/projects/ramp-combo-baryonic-pk/runs/261017_143153/ as 2410.17109.txt, 2512.02954.txt, 2309.07959.txt, 2206.11794.txt and 2309.02920.txt.

Mechanism, from those texts:
- Energy injected by AGN moves gas relative to the dark matter and suppresses small-scale power by tens of percent compared with dark-matter-only runs (2512.02954).
- Below about 10 Mpc, AGN push baryons outward, while on smaller scales star formation concentrates baryons in halo centres (2309.02920).
- In FLAMINGO (2410.17109), the response is stronger for lower group and cluster gas fractions, for collimated jets instead of thermal winds, and for lower stellar mass at fixed gas fraction.
- As redshift falls, the FLAMINGO response grows and its minimum moves to smaller scales. The dependence on cosmology is about 1 percent at k<10 h/Mpc. Its emulator is accurate to better than 1 percent up to k=10 h/Mpc and z=3.

Benchmarks at k=1 h/Mpc:
- eROSITA plus kSZ: 10 +/- 2 percent; HSC-XXL: 5 +/- 4 percent. Both are for haloes with 13<log10 M500<14 at 0<z<1 (2512.02954).
- Cluster-based baryon-correction priors (2309.02920): 0.042 (+0.012/-0.014) at k=1 h/Mpc and 0.184 (+0.026/-0.031) at k=3 h/Mpc. The effect is below 1 percent for k<0.37 h/Mpc at 97.5 percent credibility.

Weak lensing:
- KiDS-1000 shear gives S8 = 0.759 (+0.024/-0.021). This can be reconciled with Planck LCDM if nonlinear power is suppressed more strongly than simulations predict (2206.11794).
- FLAMINGO concludes that baryon physics is unlikely to be driving the S8 tension (2309.07959).
- The mitigation route demonstrated for LSST Y1 is to calibrate feedback models with multi-wavelength gas observables (2512.02954).

Citations: 2410.17109, 2309.07959 and 2206.11794 were cited with verbatim quotes into references.bib in the run directory.

result.summary:
Three papers were read and cited with verbatim quotes in /Users/nramachandra/hep-genesis-testing/projects/ramp-combo-baryonic-pk/runs/261017_143153/references.bib.

(1) Amon & Efstathiou (2206.11794): KiDS-1000 cosmic shear is consistent with Planck LCDM if non-linear power is suppressed with A_mod ~ 0.69. The suppression must extend to k ~ 0.2 h/Mpc, which is well outside the BAHAMAS range.

(2) FLAMINGO (2309.07959): across its range of feedback variants, baryonic effects are not large enough to remove the S8 tension; the paper says 'it is unlikely that baryon physics is driving this modification'.

(3) Siegel et al. (2512.02954): joint eROSITA and kSZ data give 10+/-2% suppression at k=1 h/Mpc, while HSC-XXL gives 5+/-4%. Only the strong-feedback runs BAHAMAS 8.0 and FLAMINGO fgas-8sigma agree with the eROSITA and kSZ result, and the simulations differ from each other by more than 10% at k=1 h/Mpc. Mitigation, from their LSST Y1-like mock (Fig. 6 of that paper): with no baryon model, S8 is significantly biased. An uninformed baryonification model removes the bias but halves the precision. A prior calibrated on kSZ and eROSITA recovers half of the lost precision. The paper reports this bias only graphically and gives no numerical S8 shift.

Findings f-004 (the literature numbers) and f-005 (qualitative comparison framework) are posted. The comparison with d-01 is only a framework so far, because the d-01 emulator values at k=1 h/Mpc were not on the board when I posted. No lensing quantity was computed. 2305.09827, 2206.08591 and 2410.12500 were not read.

This direction is partly done. The parameter bounds, the sensitivity ranking and the 5%/10% check were completed. The suppression minimum is not resolved above k=3.73 h/Mpc, and the comparison plot was not made. Results are in f-013, f-014 and f-015, and the dead end is x-01.

Parameter bounds, quoted from describe_parameters (f-013):
- kappa_w is the 'AGN wind coupling / wind efficiency parameter', range [2, 4].
- e_w is the 'AGN energy efficiency / wind energy fraction', range [0.2, 1].
- M_seed is in units of 1e6 Msun, range [0.6, 2].
- v_kin is in units of 1e4 km/s, range [0.1, 1.2].
- eps_kin is in units of 10, range [0.02, 1.2].
- omega_m is Omega_m h^2, range [0.12, 0.155].
- sigma_8 has range [0.7, 0.9].

New z=0 Pk-ratio runs, each with all other parameters at the fiducial point:
- kappa_w=2: suppression 2.92+/-0.15% at k=1, 10.93+/-0.54% at k=3 and 13.66% at k=3.71 h/Mpc.
- kappa_w=4: 1.31+/-0.13% at k=1 and 4.95+/-0.46% at k=3 h/Mpc.
- M_seed=2.0: 2.42+/-0.14% at k=1 and 9.03+/-0.49% at k=3 h/Mpc.
- Fiducial, for reference: 2.17% at k=1 and 8.03% at k=3 h/Mpc.
Lower kappa_w strengthens suppression.

Sensitivity ranking (f-014):
- At k=1: lowering e_w, v_kin and eps_kin together (-2.4 pp) > kappa_w (1.6 pp spread across its range) > raising e_w, v_kin and eps_kin together (+0.33 pp) > M_seed (+0.25 pp).
- At k=3: kappa_w (6.0 pp spread across its range) > M_seed (+1.0 pp) > raising e_w, v_kin and eps_kin together (+0.76 pp).
- At k=3 every shift exceeds the emulator 1-sigma of 0.35-0.54%. At k=1 the M_seed and joint-raising shifts are only about 2 sigma.

Observational comparison, restricted to the six sampled points (f-015, which restates f-002):
- No sampled point reaches 5% or 10% suppression at k=1 h/Mpc; the maximum is 2.9% at kappa_w=2.
- That point is about 0.5 sigma from HSC-XXL (5+/-4%) and falls short of eROSITA+kSZ (10+/-2%) by about 3.5 sigma.
- At k=3 h/Mpc the largest sampled value, 10.9%, falls short of the 18.4% from 2309.02920 by about 2.4 sigma.
- Combined extremes, such as kappa_w=2 together with strong e_w, v_kin, eps_kin and M_seed, were not sampled.

Unresolved above k=3.73 h/Mpc (x-01): every curve is still deepening at k=3.73 h/Mpc, so no values at k=5 or 10 h/Mpc, no minimum and no high-k upturn were obtained. The cause is that read_text_file truncates the 799-bin CSVs. The comparison plot was not made because the budget ran out.

result.summary: Two sourcing gaps are closed, with verbatim quotes stored in /Users/nramachandra/hep-genesis-testing/projects/ramp-combo-baryonic-pk/runs/261017_143153/references.bib; the depth of the FLAMINGO z=0 minimum is still open. (1) 2309.02920 (key arxiv230902920), finding f-009: suppression of 0.042 (+0.012/-0.014) at k=1 h/Mpc and 0.184 (+0.026/-0.031) at k=3 h/Mpc in the fiducial model, or 0.049 and 0.179 in the alternative model; at 97.5% credibility the impact is below 1% for k<0.37 h/Mpc. (2) 2410.17109 (key arxiv241017109), finding f-010: the FLAMINGO fiducial minimum moves from k=6 h/Mpc at z=2 to k=10 h/Mpc at z=0. For thermal-AGN fgas variants from -10 to +4 sigma it stays at k=8-10 h/Mpc, and fgas mostly changes the amplitude. The response saturates below fgas-8sigma, and the jet model has a similar k-range. The text gives no number for the minimum depth; it is shown only in the paper's own Figs. 2, 5 and 6, so it remains open as q-08. (3) Comparison table, finding f-011, which replaces f-005. Suppression at k=1 / k=3 h/Mpc: HACC fiducial 2.2% / 8.0%; HACC strong 2.5% / 8.8%; 2309.02920 4.2% / 18.4%; HSC-XXL 5+/-4% at k=1; eROSITA+kSZ 10+/-2% at k=1. At k=1, HACC is consistent with HSC-XXL and about 1.3 sigma below 2309.02920. At k=3, HACC is low by a factor of about 2.1-2.3, or about 3.1-3.4 sigma, even at the edge of its design range. This gap is flagged as unexplained. Possible contributors: the HACC curve shape (minimum above k=3.7 h/Mpc, against 8-10 h/Mpc in FLAMINGO), the P_grav reference, differences in cosmology and halo-mass weighting, and kappa_w and M_seed held fixed. No more strongly suppressed d-03 or d-05 point was available to add. (4) Correction to f-004, finding f-012: A_mod~0.69 is sufficient to reconcile KiDS with Planck, not the only route. An uninformed baryonification model roughly doubles the S8 uncertainty, and a kSZ+eROSITA prior recovers about half of that loss. Open question q-08: the numerical depth of the FLAMINGO minimum, and whether varying kappa_w and M_seed lets HACC reach about 18% suppression at k=3.

result.summary: Partly done. Three success criteria are not met: (1) the DES Y3 A_mod number was not found; (2) nothing was run through cite, so 2305.09827 and 2410.12500 are not in references.bib; (3) no theta range was sourced. What was established, from full texts saved in /Users/nramachandra/hep-genesis-testing/projects/ramp-combo-baryonic-pk/runs/261017_143153/ (2305.09827.txt, 2410.12500.txt): (a) Finding f-006. For DES Y3, Preston, Amon & Efstathiou (2305.09827) use the model P_m = P_L + A_mod(P_NL - P_L). They find the suppression needed to resolve the S8 tension 'is not as strong as inferred using KiDS data' (KiDS A_mod ~ 0.69) 'but is still more extreme than predictions from recent numerical simulations'. It must extend to k ~ 0.2 h/Mpc. I quoted this from the abstract but did not read the numerical DES A_mod. (b) Finding f-007. As a second mitigation method, Maraio, Hall & Taylor (2410.12500) put a theoretical-error covariance into the matter power spectrum in place of ell scale cuts. With ell_max = 5000 for a Euclid-like survey, it reduces the bias in Omega_m and S8 to acceptable levels with a modest increase in variance. The first mitigation method, multi-wavelength calibration from 2512.02954, is already in f-004. The only ell range sourced is that the baryon-sensitive shear goes up to ell ~ 5000. (c) Finding f-008, an approximate comparison only. The HACC emulator suppression is about 0.8-0.9% at k=0.5 h/Mpc and at most 2.5% at k=1 h/Mpc. This is far below the A_mod-level suppression reaching k ~ 0.2 h/Mpc, so within its design range the emulator cannot approach the suppression needed to reconcile shear with Planck. A C_ell or xi_+ lensing forecast is flagged as future work, which answers q-03.

result.summary: The direction is mostly done, with three gaps. First, the fiducial z=0 and z=1 values were written to CSV but not read, so the z=0 vs z=1 comparison so far covers only one parameter point. Second, the maxsupp_lowkin and maxsupp_lowM variants were plotted but their values were not read, so it is still untested whether the kinetic parameters or M_seed act non-monotonically. Third, only one of the two planned plots survives. Results: the Pk-ratio emulator is trained at z = 0, 0.1, 0.5, 1.0 and 2.0, and its design bounds are in f-016. At z=0 the combined extreme point (kappa_w=2, e_w=1.0, M_seed=2.0, v_kin=1.2, eps_kin=1.2, omega_m=0.14, sigma_8=0.8) gives P_hydro/P_grav = 0.99944+/-0.00003 at k=0.10, 0.9868+/-0.0008 at k=0.51, 0.9638+/-0.0020 at k=1.01, 0.9179+/-0.0045 at k=2.0, 0.8698+/-0.0065 at k=3.0 and 0.8400+/-0.0076 at k=3.7 h/Mpc. That is a suppression of 3.6+/-0.2% at k=1 and 13.0+/-0.7% at k=3 (f-024). Comparisons: consistent with HSC-XXL (0.35 sigma); short of eROSITA+kSZ by 3.2 sigma; below 2309.02920 by 0.6 points at k=1 and 5.4 points at k=3, counting emulator error only. The extreme point reaches neither 10% at k=1 nor 18% at k=3. It is the strongest suppression found here, but the low-kinetic and low-M_seed variants were not read out, so it is not shown to be the maximum over the whole design range. Redshift trend for the extreme point (f-027): suppression drops from z=0 to z=1, from 3.6% to 2.2% at k=1 and from 13.0% to 7.0% at k=3. This agrees with FLAMINGO's finding that the response grows as z falls. The ratio is still falling at k=3.7 at both redshifts, so the shift of the minimum could not be tested. 3. strongAGN point (kappa_w=3, e_w=1.0, v_kin=1.2, eps_kin=1.2, omega_m=0.14, sigma_8=0.8), z=0 (finding f-017). P_hydro/P_grav is 0.851 at k=5.25, 0.8205 at k=7.01, 0.7946 (std 0.0098) at k=10.01 and 0.7893 at k=12.55 h/Mpc. The curve flattens to a plateau of about 0.789-0.790 over k of about 11.6-12.6 h/Mpc. FLAMINGO's minimum is at k of about 8-10 h/Mpc; HACC's falls at k of 12 h/Mpc or higher, but it is not resolved.

The matching strongAGN values are 0.9746, 0.9121 and 0.8909, so strong kinetic feedback adds only about 0.3-0.8 percentage points of suppression over this range. Their files exist under runs/261017_143153/ in folders of the same names, and their headers were checked.

Two of the three targets are met. The FLAMINGO z=0 minimum depth (q-08) is still open.

q-07 answered (f-025): Preston, Amon and Efstathiou (arXiv:2305.09827, Eq. 3) give A_mod = 0.858 +/- 0.052 for DES Y3 with no scale cuts and a Planck prior on S8 and Omega_m. The verbatim quote is 'Amod = 0.858± 0.052, DES Y3 (no scale cuts)' (tc-...-57). For comparison, KiDS-1000 in Paper I gave A_mod ≈ 0.69 (tc-...-41). The same paper says the suppression must extend to k ~ 0.2 h/Mpc. Without A_mod, DES Y3 S8 sits 0.9 sigma (variant 3) to 1.8 sigma (variant 4) below Planck S8 = 0.828 +/- 0.016.

Other results:
- f-020: Siegel et al. (arXiv:2512.02954) find 10 +/- 2% suppression at k = 1 h/Mpc from eROSITA plus kSZ data, stronger than fiducial FLAMINGO and BAHAMAS. HSC-XXL data give 5 +/- 4%.

result.summary:
Only part of this direction got done. I have one numerical cosmology bias from ignoring baryons, but it is an Omega_m bias, not an S8 bias, and I did not read the HACC values at k=0.2-0.3 h/Mpc.

What was established:

1. Omega_m bias from Maraio, Hall and Taylor (arXiv:2410.12500, Table 3), read verbatim (f-031; tc-...-86). Survey configuration: an idealised Euclid-like Stage-IV cosmic-shear survey with ell_max = 5000.
- Illustris as ground truth, analysed with the one-parameter HMCode model and no theory error: 100*Delta Omega_m = -1.317, which is -5.69 sigma.
- The same case with the theoretical-error covariance added: 0.128, or 0.249 sigma.
- Bahamas as ground truth with the one-parameter model: 0.057, or 0.258 sigma.
- Eagle with the six-parameter model and the theory error included: still 0.573, or 1.459 sigma.
- The text says the one-parameter model without theory error gives at least a 3 sigma offset in either Omega_m or S8 for every hydro simulation except Bahamas. For Simba as ground truth, even ell_max = 1000 is biased by more than 2 sigma in all parameters.
- The full text is saved at runs/261023_143127/2410.12500.txt. The Delta S8 values are in Table 4, past character 55000 of that file, and I did not read them.

2. HACC maxsupp z=0 Pk-ratio beyond k=3.7 h/Mpc (f-032; tc-...-83). Values are 0.8284 at k=4.0, 0.7942 at k=5.0, 0.7680 at k=6.0, 0.7479 at k=7.0 and 0.7356 at k=7.84 h/Mpc. This is already deeper than the strongAGN plateau of about 0.789 (f-017).
- Source file: runs/261023_143127/maxsupp_z0/Pk-ratio_z0.0000_prediction.csv.

3. HACC suppression versus the A_mod requirement: this comparison is qualitative only, since the k=0.2-0.3 values are unread.
- From f-024, S(k) goes from 0.9994 at k=0.10 to 0.987 at k=0.51 h/Mpc, so at k~0.2 it is presumably below 1%.
- That is consistent with Grandis et al.'s bound of less than 1% for k < 0.37 h/Mpc.
- It is far weaker than the suppression that A_mod = 0.858+/-0.052 (DES Y3) or about 0.69 (KiDS-1000) would need at k~0.2 h/Mpc.
- On this basis, HACC-level feedback is unlikely to resolve S8. That conclusion rests on interpolation, not on read-out values.

No figures were produced.

findings.claim: Literature synthesis from full texts that were read: (1) Mechanism: energy from active galactic nuclei (AGN) moves gas relative to the dark matter. This suppresses the nonlinear matter power by tens of percent compared with dark-matter-only runs (2512.02954). Below about 10 Mpc, AGN redistribute baryons outward, while on smaller scales star formation concentrates baryons in halo centres (2309.02920). In FLAMINGO, lower group and cluster gas fractions, collimated jets instead of thermal winds, and lower stellar mass at fixed gas fraction all strengthen the response. As z falls, the response grows and its minimum moves to smaller scales. The cosmology dependence is about 1 percent at k<10 h/Mpc (2410.17109). (2) Benchmarks: suppression at k=1 h/Mpc is 10+/-2 percent from eROSITA plus kSZ and 5+/-4 percent from HSC-XXL, over 13<log10 M500/(Msun/h)<14 and 0<z<1 (2512.02954). Cluster baryon-correction-model priors give 0.042 (+0.012/-0.014) at k=1 h/Mpc and 0.184 (+0.026/-0.031) at k=3 h/Mpc, with less than 1 percent impact at k<0.37 h/Mpc at 97.5 percent credibility (2309.02920). (3) Weak lensing: Amon and Efstathiou find that KiDS-1000 (S8 = 0.759 +0.024/-0.021) can be reconciled with Planck LCDM if nonlinear power is suppressed more strongly than simulations predict (2206.11794). FLAMINGO finds baryonic effects are not large enough to remove the S8 tension (2309.07959). Mitigation is to calibrate feedback with multi-wavelength gas observables (2512.02954).

findings.claim: Preston, Amon & Efstathiou (2305.09827) find that to reconcile DES Y3 cosmic shear with Planck LCDM, the non-linear suppression needed is weaker than the KiDS-1000 value (A_mod ~ 0.69). findings.claim: Second mitigation method (Maraio, Hall & Taylor, 2410.12500): a theoretical-error covariance built into the matter power spectrum, used in place of binary ell scale cuts. For a Euclid-like survey with ell_max = 5000, even multi-parameter baryon models can introduce significant bias. The theoretical error reduces the bias in Omega_m and S8 to acceptable levels with only a modest increase in variance, and it removes the need to choose an ell_max for each bin. This places the baryon-sensitive shear range up to ell ~ 5000.

findings.claim: Approximate comparison only. The HACC emulator gives about 0.8-0.9% suppression at k=0.5 h/Mpc, about 0.03-0.04% at k=0.1 h/Mpc and at most 2.5% at k=1 h/Mpc (f-001, f-002). This is far below the A_mod-type suppression that Amon-Efstathiou and Preston et al. require. That suppression scales the whole non-linear part of P(k) (A_mod ~ 0.69 for KiDS, weaker but still beyond simulations for DES) and reaches down to k ~ 0.2 h/Mpc. Within its design range, the emulator cannot approach the suppression needed to reconcile shear with Planck. A projected C_ell or xi_+ forecast is future work, since no tool computes it.

findings.claim: FLAMINGO (2410.17109, quoted and cited as arxiv241017109). For the fiducial model, the minimum of P/P_DMO moves from k=6 h/Mpc at z=2 to k=10 h/Mpc at z=0. The jet model has a stronger response at negative fgas but a similar k-range and minimum position. The text gives no numerical depth for the z=0 minimum: it appears only in Figs. 2, 5 and 6 of the paper, whose y-axes run from 0.75 to 1.10. Both fgas-8sigma models (thermal and jet) fall inside the ranges of Bigwood et al. 2024, with or without kSZ. The Amon & Efstathiou 2022 response is out of reach of the FLAMINGO emulator.

findings.claim: Grandis et al. (arXiv:2309.02920) use cluster gas and stellar fractions to infer a suppression of 0.042 (+0.012/-0.014) at k = 1 h/Mpc and 0.184 (+0.026/-0.031) at k = 3 h/Mpc. They predict, at 97.5% credibility, that baryons change P(k) by less than 1% for k < 0.37 h/Mpc, and on that basis question whether baryon feedback drives the cosmic-shear vs CMB S8 discrepancy.

Preston, Amon and Efstathiou (arXiv:2305.09827) model P_m = P_L + A_mod (P_NL - P_L). Their KiDS-1000 Paper I value is A_mod ≈ 0.69. For DES Y3 the abstract says only that the required suppression is "not as strong as inferred using KiDS data, but is still more extreme than predictions from recent numerical simulations", and that it must extend to k ~ 0.2 h/Mpc. The DES Y3 numerical A_mod was not in the portion of the text read so far.

Maraio, Hall and Taylor (arXiv:2410.12500) find that for a Euclid-like survey with ell_max = 5000, even multi-parameter baryon models (including HMCode-2020) can bias Omega_m and S8 significantly. A theoretical-error covariance on P(k) reduces this bias to acceptable levels with only a modest increase in parameter variances. The abstract gives no numerical S8 shift.

At z=0 the combined extreme HACC point (kappa_w=2, e_w=1.0, M_seed=2.0, v_kin=1.2, eps_kin=1.2, omega_m=0.14, sigma_8=0.8) gives P_hydro/P_grav = 0.99944+/-0.00003 at k=0.101, 0.9868+/-0.0008 at k=0.510, 0.9638+/-0.0020 at k=1.013, 0.9179+/-0.0045 at k=2.002, 0.8698+/-0.0065 at k=3.007 and 0.8400+/-0.0076 at k=3.698 h/Mpc. That is a suppression of 3.6+/-0.2% at k=1 and 13.0+/-0.7% at k=3. Against HSC-XXL (5+/-4% at k=1) the gap is 0.35 sigma, so the point is consistent. Against eROSITA+kSZ (10+/-2% at k=1) it falls short by 3.2 sigma. Against 2309.02920 (4.2% at k=1, 18.4% at k=3) it is 0.6 points low at k=1 (about 3 sigma of emulator error alone) and 5.4 points low at k=3 (about 8 sigma of emulator error alone). This point reaches neither 10% at k=1 nor 18% at k=3.

Maraio, Hall and Taylor (arXiv:2410.12500, Table 3) work with an idealised Euclid-like (Stage-IV) cosmic-shear survey at ell_max = 5000 and use Illustris as the ground truth. When the one-parameter HMCode baryon model is fitted without a theory error, Omega_m is biased by 100*Delta Omega_m = -1.317, which is -5.690 sigma. Adding the theoretical-error covariance cuts this to 0.128 (0.249 sigma). With Bahamas as the ground truth the bias is only 0.057 (0.258 sigma). Eagle with the 6-parameter model is still biased with the theory error included: 0.573 (1.459 sigma). In the text, the one-parameter model without theory error gives 'at least a 3 sigma offset in either Omega_m or S8 for all hydro-sims excluding Bahamas'. For Simba, even ell_max = 1000 is biased by more than 2 sigma in all cosmological parameters.

findings.claim: For the combined extreme point, the HACC maxsupp z=0 Pk-ratio keeps falling past k=3.7 h/Mpc: 0.8284+/-0.0079 at k=4.00, 0.7942+/-0.0089 at k=5.00, 0.7680+/-0.0095 at k=6.0, 0.7479+/-0.0100 at k=7.01 and 0.7356 at k=7.84 h/Mpc. That is already deeper than the strongAGN plateau of about 0.789 at k of about 12 h/Mpc (f-017), so kappa_w=2 with M_seed=2.0 gives more small-scale suppression than kappa_w=3. The values at k=0.2-0.3 h/Mpc were not read within the budget.

The HACC fGas emulator at z=0 has 3 M500c bins: 5.01e13, 7.94e13 and 1.26e14 Msun/h. In the bin nearest 1e14 (1.26e14 Msun/h), f_gas = 0.1214+/-0.0010 for fiducial, 0.1221+/-0.0019 for strongAGN and 0.1414+/-0.0023 for weakAGN (e_w=0.2, v_kin=0.1, eps_kin=0.02). At 7.94e13 Msun/h the values are 0.1090, 0.1098 and 0.1375.

Partial answer to q-12. Only two fGas points have S(k) read so far. Fiducial: f_gas(1.26e14) = 0.1214+/-0.0010, with S(k=1) = 0.9779 and S(k=3) = 0.9197. StrongAGN: f_gas = 0.1221+/-0.0019, with S(k=1) = 0.9746 and S(k=3) = 0.9121. The two f_gas values agree within errors; strongAGN is nominally higher, yet its suppression is 0.3-0.8 points deeper. Between these two points there is therefore no resolvable van Daalen-type relation, and the nominal trend runs the wrong way. WeakAGN has a much higher f_gas (0.1414), but its S(k) was not read in this direction, so a three-point test is still open. The strongAGN vs fiducial comparison is confounded: e_w changes (0.6 to 1.0) at the same time as v_kin and eps_kin.

The HACC maxsupp_lowkin point at z=0 (kappa_w=2, e_w=1.0, M_seed=2.0, v_kin=0.1, eps_kin=0.02, omega_m=0.14, sigma_8=0.8) shows essentially no suppression. P_hydro/P_grav is 1.0002 at k=0.212, 1.0004+/-0.0007 at k=0.510, 1.0006+/-0.0019 at k=1.013, 1.0033+/-0.0042 at k=2.002, 0.9972+/-0.0062 at k=3.007 and 0.9883+/-0.0071 at k=3.698 h/Mpc. So in this emulator the kinetic AGN parameters (v_kin, eps_kin) drive almost all of the suppression at k up to 3.7 h/Mpc, even with e_w at its maximum.

The HACC maxsupp_lowM point at z=0 (kappa_w=2, e_w=1.0, M_seed=0.6, v_kin=1.2, eps_kin=1.2, omega_m=0.14, sigma_8=0.8) suppresses more than the combined maxsupp point (M_seed=2.0). P_hydro/P_grav is 0.9967 at k=0.212, 0.9835+/-0.0011 at k=0.510, 0.9557+/-0.0029 at k=1.013, 0.9026+/-0.0064 at k=2.002, 0.8521+/-0.0094 at k=3.007 and 0.8228+/-0.0109 at k=3.698 h/Mpc. The maxsupp values are 0.9638, 0.8698 and 0.8400 at k=1, 3 and 3.7. The suppression is 4.4+/-0.3% at k=1 and 14.8+/-0.9% at k=3, so maxsupp is not the strongest point, and low M_seed increases the suppression. This is still short of eROSITA+kSZ (10+/-2% at k=1, arXiv:2512.02954) by about 2.8 sigma. It is consistent with HSC-XXL (5+/-4%) and with Grandis et al. at k=1 (4.2%). At k=3 it is 3.6 points below Grandis (18.4%). Among the points read, the HACC design range does not reach the eROSITA+kSZ level at k=1.

questions.text: Does the HACC emulator's Pk-ratio k range reach 10 h/Mpc and beyond, so that the suppression minimum and the upturn at higher k are actually covered? If the range is truncated, the report must state it.
Which emulator parameters map most directly onto AGN feedback strength, and do their ranges span suppression levels comparable to both the HSC-XXL and the eROSITA plus kSZ constraints at k=1 h/Mpc?
The S8 impact will come from the literature rather than our own shear forecast, because no tool computes C_ell or xi_plus. Should a projected-lensing estimate be flagged as future work?
Are the emulator's uncertainties at z=0 small compared with the differences between feedback variants, so that the conclusions are meaningful?

Still open from d-02: four items were not covered. (1) The exact depth and k of FLAMINGO's z=0 suppression minimum, from the body or figures of 2410.17109. (2) Extraction of the 2410.17109 figure comparing feedback variants. (3) The S8 shift or suppression amplitude that Amon and Efstathiou require. (4) Citations, with quotes, for 2512.02954 and 2309.02920, which were read but not yet run through cite.

Can someone with a proper CSV reader extract the ratio at k=5 and 10 h/Mpc, the minimum and its k, and whether kappa_w (held at 3) gives stronger suppression than e_w, v_kin and eps_kin?

What is the numerical DES Y3 A_mod fitted by Preston et al. (2305.09827)? It is in the body text, chars 6000-48000 of runs/261017_143153/2305.09827.txt, which was not read. Also, can 2305.09827 and 2410.12500 be run through cite using the abstract quotes in f-006 and f-007?

What is the numerical depth of the FLAMINGO fiducial (and fgas-8sigma) z=0 P/P_DMO minimum near k=10 h/Mpc? It is only shown graphically in Figs. 2 and 5 of 2410.17109, so it needs figure extraction or the public FLAMINGO emulator. Does the HACC emulator, with kappa_w and M_seed varied, reach the 2309.02920 value of about 18% suppression at k=3 h/Mpc?
Does HACC's Pk-ratio use a P_grav reference that differs from P_DMO in the other emulators, and could that explain the factor of about 2 deficit at k=3 h/Mpc?
Is the HACC design range too narrow to span the feedback strength now favoured by kSZ and eROSITA, and should the final report say so explicitly?
No coding tool is available. Should the lensing impact stay a literature-based assessment, with the C_ell or xi_+ forecast explicitly listed as future work?

What are the fGas values at M500c of about 1e14 Msun/h in the three fGas CSVs under runs/261023_143127/fgas_*, and do they fall monotonically as the k=1 and k=3 suppression grows (fiducial 0.978/0.920, strongAGN 0.975/0.912), as van Daalen et al. 1906.00968 would predict?

Using read_arxiv_chunk on the downloaded .txt files in runs/261023_143127/, can someone confirm verbatim the 10+/-2% and 5+/-4% values (2512.02954) and the 0.042 and 0.184 values (2309.02920), and quote the FLAMINGO z=0 S(k=1) and the depth and k of its minimum (2410.17109)?

Two values are still unread. First, the maxsupp_z0 S(k) at k=0.2-0.3 h/Mpc (CSV chars about 0-3000). From f-024 it lies between 0.9994 at k=0.1 and 0.987 at k=0.51, so it is likely below 1%, which is far weaker than an A_mod of 0.86 (DES Y3) or 0.69 (KiDS) would need at k~0.2. Second, Table 4 (Delta S8) of 2410.12500 at text chars >55000. Separately, a Limber C_ell / S8 Fisher forecast using HACC S(k) remains future work.

contested.reason: The claim that the k=1 h/Mpc suppression 'across the full design range of the AGN and kinetic parameters' spans only about -0.2% to +2.5% is not supported. Only three corner-like points were run. kappa_w (fixed at 3), M_seed and cosmology were never varied, and the parameter bounds were not shown in any cited evidence (no describe_parameters output). The quoted CSV excerpts (tc-...-49, -31, -37) also stop at k=0.117 h/Mpc. The peak of 1.0097 near k=2.4 and the k=1 and k=3.71 values are not visible in the evidence; only the k=0.101 value (1.00009) can be checked. The weak-point measurements may be right, but the design-range generalisation must be removed or backed by a parameter scan.

Every evidence excerpt is the title and author header (chars 0-4000) of a paper. None contains the specific numbers claimed: 10+/-2 and 5+/-4 percent, 0.042 and 0.184 at k=1 and 3 h/Mpc, k<0.37 at 97.5 percent, S8=0.759, or about 1 percent cosmology dependence. 2309.02920 was never cited through the cite tool, so no verbatim quote is stored for its numbers. The numbers are plausible and partly corroborated by f-004 for 2512.02954, but this finding's own evidence does not contain them.

issues.text: The quoted CSV excerpts stop at k=0.117 h/Mpc. The values at k=0.51, 1, 2, 3 and 3.71 are not visible in the cited evidence; only the k=0.101 values (0.99968 fiducial, 0.99962 strong) can be checked. The k=1 values are the key numbers of the task and should be re-extracted with a working reader and quoted directly (q-06). The finding is accepted on the summary's account, but this is a weak point.

Wording of the comparison. The phrase 'eROSITA+kSZ ... excluded at more than 3.5 sigma' reverses the logic. The emulator cannot exclude a measurement. The correct statement is that the sampled HACC points fall short of the eROSITA+kSZ value by about 3.7 sigma (observational error only). The comparison also mixes a fixed HACC cosmology (omega_m=0.14, probably omega_m h^2) with observational constraints derived under a different cosmology and halo-mass weighting. It should be framed as a range-of-model check, as critique c-01 required.

There is a physics discrepancy no one has noted. At k=3 h/Mpc the HACC fiducial and strong points give about 8-9 percent suppression, while the cluster-calibrated prior of 2309.02920 gives 18.4 percent (+2.6/-3.1). At k=1 the emulator gives 2.2-2.5 percent against 4.2 percent there and 5-10 percent from 2512.02954. In addition, the weak-AGN point shows a net enhancement, and the strong AGN parameters barely matter (0.3 percentage points). Together these suggest that the parameters held fixed (kappa_w, M_seed), or the parameter interpretation itself, control most of the suppression. This must be resolved before any conclusion about feedback strength.

Two sourcing gaps remain (q-05). 2309.02920 has no stored citation or quote. The depth and k of FLAMINGO's z=0 minimum, which the brief listed as a quantity to check, is still unsourced, and so are the 1104.1174 claims of a 10-30 percent minimum at 5-20 h/Mpc and the high-k upturn.

'Consistent with Planck LCDM only if' is stronger than the source. Amon and Efstathiou show that suppression with A_mod about 0.69 is sufficient, not that it is the only route. 'Costs 2x in precision' should be stated precisely: the S8 uncertainty roughly doubles.
f-005 was written before the d-01 numbers were available and is now stale. It should be replaced by an explicit comparison table: HACC at k=1 and k=3 versus 2309.02920, HSC-XXL and eROSITA+kSZ.

No weak-lensing quantity has been estimated. The task asks for the impact on weak-lensing cosmology. A rough projected estimate (which ell range is affected, and the order of magnitude of the xi_+ or C_ell suppression) can be sourced from 1910.11357 or 2305.09827, or derived approximately from the emulator curve. Either must be clearly labelled as such.

contested.reason: The only evidence (tc-261017_1-w2-d-07-73) is the title and author header of 2410.12500. The claimed specifics are not in the excerpt: ell_max = 5000, a Euclid-like survey, bias in Omega_m and S8 reduced to acceptable levels, and a modest increase in variance. No cite call with verbatim quotes was made (d-07 says cite was never run). The title supports only the method itself, a theoretical-error covariance.

The statement 'at most 2.5% at k=1 h/Mpc' is contradicted by f-014 in the same wave, where kappa_w=2 gives 2.92+/-0.15%. The conclusion that 'within its design range the emulator cannot approach' the required suppression overreaches: f-015 states that combined extremes were not sampled. The comparison is also not like-for-like. A_mod scales P_NL - P_L, so the implied 1 - P/P_DMO at k = 0.2-1 h/Mpc must be computed before it can be set against HACC ratios. None of the evidence contains that conversion.

The k=3 conclusion, 'low by a factor of about 2.1-2.3, or about 3.1-3.4 sigma, even at the edge of the HACC design range', is superseded by f-014 and f-015. The kappa_w=2 point gives 10.9% at k=3, about 2.4 sigma below 18.4% (lower error 3.1). The fiducial and strong points held kappa_w and M_seed fixed, so they are not at the edge of the design range. The arithmetic for the fiducial and strong points is correct. The 2309.02920 values rest on a title-only excerpt here and are carried over from f-009.

issues.text: The quoted phrases 'not as strong as inferred using KiDS data' and 'k ~ 0.2 h/Mpc' are attributed to the abstract, but the excerpt from tc-...-72 is cut off after the author affiliations. Only the conclusions chunk (tc-...-78) visibly supports 'stronger than favoured in recent hydrodynamic simulations'. The DES Y3 A_mod value is still unsourced, and 2305.09827 is not cited.

The visible excerpts support the fgas range from -10 to +4 sigma and the statement that only Illustris and cosmo-OWLS 8.7 are out of reach. The excerpts do not show the minimum positions (k=6 at z=2, k=10 at z=0), the saturation below fgas-8sigma, the Bigwood et al. compatibility, or the claim that Amon & Efstathiou is out of reach. These rest on the cite call. The depth of the FLAMINGO minimum is still open (q-08), and it is the benchmark most needed for comparing curve shapes.

The excerpts for every CSV are cut off at k of about 0.12 h/Mpc, so the k=1 and k=3 values cannot be checked against the quoted evidence. They are internally consistent with each other and with f-001. e_w, v_kin and eps_kin were only moved jointly, so their individual sensitivities are unknown. omega_m and sigma_8 were never varied, so the claimed cosmology independence of about 1% (FLAMINGO) has not been checked for HACC.

The task asks for the shape of the suppression up to about 10 h/Mpc, including the depth and position of the minimum, and this is still not delivered. All runs are still deepening at k=3.7 h/Mpc because of the CSV truncation (x-01, q-06). Without the curve above 3.7 h/Mpc, the comparison of minimum position against FLAMINGO (8-10 h/Mpc) and the explanation of the factor-2 gap at k=3 remain speculative.

f-002 is still contested on the board. Its claim that the k=1 suppression spans -0.2% to +2.5% across the full AGN design range is falsified by kappa_w=2 (2.92%). It should be formally retired in favour of f-015.

The weak-lensing assessment has no projected quantity. There is no C_ell or xi_+ suppression and no S8 shift. The only ell range comes from an unverified f-007 statement (ell_max = 5000). The lensing-weighted redshift of about 0.3-0.5 was never probed, since all HACC runs are at z=0.

The full texts are already on disk, so checking them is cheap. Until it is done, the headline conclusion that HACC falls short of eROSITA+kSZ by about 3 sigma is provisional.

The emulator values for lowM are supported. The comparisons to Siegel et al. and Grandis et al. inherit the contested status of f-020 and f-021. The claim that 'the design range does not reach eROSITA+kSZ' has only been tested at the kappa_w=2, e_w=1 corners with omega_m=0.14 and sigma_8=0.8. The lowM curve is still falling at k=3.7, so its minimum is unresolved. The cosmology axes (omega_m 0.12-0.155, sigma_8 0.7-0.9) were not explored, and they can shift the response through the baryon fraction and halo abundance.

There is a physically interesting signal here that the finding does not develop. Strong kinetic feedback leaves f_gas(<R500c) at 1.26e14 essentially unchanged (0.1214 vs 0.1221), yet it deepens S(k). That suggests the HACC suppression is driven by gas removal beyond R500c, or by other halo masses, rather than by the R500c gas fraction. A controlled single-parameter sweep is needed to test this.

Attributing the deeper suppression to 'kappa_w=2 vs kappa_w=3' is confounded, because M_seed also differs (2.0 vs 1.3). Note too that f-036 shows lower M_seed increases suppression. That makes the kappa_w attribution plausible, but it has not been isolated by changing one parameter at a time.

There is no Delta S8 value (Table 4 of 2410.12500 is unread), the HACC k=0.2-0.3 values are interpolated rather than read, and there is no A_mod-equivalent number for any HACC point. Survey recent work on baryonic suppression of the matter power spectrum. Use the hydrodynamics emulator tools to predict the Pk-ratio at z=0 for a couple of parameter points, explain the AGN feedback physics of suppression, and assess the impact on weak-lensing cosmology.

**Survey** — 52 tools on 5 servers, 7 read-only probes, 20 papers found.

Note first: I have no hydrodynamics or baryonic emulator tool. My only tools were arXiv and web search, so I did not compute any z=0 Pk-ratio (P_hydro/P_DMO) values. Any numbers for specific parameter points have to come from running BACCO (2011.15018), BCemu (2108.08863), HMcode-2020 (2009.01858) or the van Daalen et al. power-spectrum library (1906.00968) locally. I give no suppression amplitudes because I did not read results beyond titles and short abstracts. Physics: AGN feedback, and stellar feedback in lower-mass haloes, pushes gas out of group- and cluster-mass haloes (about 1e13-1e14.5 Msun). This lowers their baryon fraction and flattens their inner mass profiles, which suppresses P(k) at k of about 0.1-10 h/Mpc relative to dark-matter-only runs. At higher k, gas cooling and star formation push the ratio back up. Several groups (van Daalen 1906.00968, resummation model 2509.04552, Debackere 1908.05765, BAHAMAS/cosmo-OWLS 2309.06479, TNG 2511.10634) find the suppression is mainly set by the baryon fraction of group-scale haloes. That ties it to X-ray, tSZ and kSZ observables. For weak lensing, these scale-dependent changes bias S8 if left out (1105.1075, 1407.4301). Amon and Efstathiou (2206.11794, 2305.09827) argue that stronger-than-standard nonlinear suppression could reconcile KiDS and DES cosmic shear with Planck, and recent kSZ/X-ray results (FLAMINGO 2410.17109, 2602.02484) hint that feedback may be stronger than in fiducial simulations. Current mitigation options are scale cuts, marginalising over HMcode or baryonification parameters, theory-error covariances (2410.12500), and outside constraints from SZ, X-ray or FRBs (2301.02186, 2401.03510, 2501.17922).

Quantities worth checking: Pk-ratio S(k)=P_hydro/P_DMO at z=0 for k=0.1-20 h/Mpc at two or more feedback settings (e.g. HMcode log10 T_AGN=7.6 vs 8.0; BACCO M_c=1e13 vs 1e14.5 Msun/h); Scale and depth of the suppression minimum, and the k where S(k) first drops below 0.99; Halo baryon fraction at about 1e14 Msun vs the size of the suppression (van Daalen-type relation); Shift in S8 or Omega_m when lensing data are fit with a DMO model vs the baryonic model; Size of suppression needed to reconcile lensing S8 with Planck (Amon and Efstathiou amplitude parameter A_mod); Redshift dependence of S(k) between z=0 and z=1.

Strong kinetic feedback leaves f_gas(<R500c) at 1.26e14 essentially unchanged (0.1214 vs 0.1221), yet it deepens S(k). That suggests the HACC suppression is driven by gas removal beyond R500c, or by other halo masses, rather than by the R500c gas fraction. A controlled single-parameter sweep is needed to test this..

arXiv ID: 2309.02920
Title: Determining the Baryon Impact on the Matter Power Spectrum with Galaxy Clusters
Authors: Sebastian Grandis, Giovanni Arico', Aurel Schneider, Laila Linke
Year: 2023
Abstract: The redistribution of baryonic matter in massive halos through processes like active galactic nuclei feedback and star formation leads to a suppression of the matter power spectrum on small scales. This redistribution can be measured empirically via the gas and stellar mass fractions in galaxy clusters, and leaves imprints on their electron density profiles. We constrain two semi-analytical baryon correction models with a compilation of recent Bayesian population studies of galaxy groups and clusters sampling a mass range above $\sim 3 \times 10^{13}$ $M_\odot$, and with cluster gas density profiles derived from deep, high-resolution X-ray observations. We are able to fit all the considered observational data, but highlight some anomalies in the observations. The constraints allow us to place precise, physically informed priors on the matter power spectrum suppression. At a scale of $k=1 h$ Mpc$^{-1}$ we find a suppression of $0.042^{+0.012}_{-0.014}$ ($0.049^{+0.016}_{-0.012}$), while at $k=3h$ Mpc$^{-1}$ we find $0.184^{+0.026}_{-0.031}$ ($0.179^{+0.018}_{-0.020}$), depending on the model used. In our fiducial setting, we also predict at 97.5 percent credibility, that at scales $k<0.37h$ Mpc$^{-1}$ baryon feedback impacts the matter power less than $1\%$. This puts into question if baryon feedback is the driving factor for the discrepancy between cosmic shear and primary CMB results. We independently confirm results on this suppression from small-scale cosmic shear studies, while we exclude some hydro-dynamical simulations with too strong and too weak baryonic feedback. Our empirical prediction of the power spectrum suppression shows that studies of galaxy groups and clusters will be instrumental in unlocking the cosmological constraining power of future cosmic shear experiments like \textit{Euclid} and Rubin-LSST, and invites further investigation of the baryon correction models.

Cosmic shear is the coherent distortion in the apparent shapes of

directly observed using telescopes. Cosmic shear is also sensitive to
the detailed physics of baryons, particularly on small scales, within
the Universe. By making accurate measurements, along with ro-
bust theoretical modelling, cosmic shear is able to provide detailed
knowledge about the physics and geometry of the universe.

turns.report:
# Baryonic suppression of the matter power spectrum: HACC emulator predictions at z = 0, AGN-feedback physics and weak-lensing impact

## Abstract

This report combines a literature survey of baryonic suppression of the matter power spectrum with predictions from a HACC-based hydrodynamics emulator. The emulator returns the ratio S(k) = P_hydro/P_grav, together with cluster gas fractions, over a 7-parameter design space: five AGN and black-hole parameters plus omega_m and sigma_8.

Main results from the emulator:

- At z = 0 the strongest suppression among the points sampled is 4.4 ± 0.3% at k = 1 h/Mpc and 14.8 ± 0.9% at k = 3 h/Mpc. It comes from maximal kinetic feedback, maximal e_w, kappa_w = 2 and the lowest seed mass.
- Kinetic AGN feedback produces almost all of the suppression. With the kinetic parameters set low, S(k) stays within about 1% of unity up to k = 3.7 h/Mpc.
- The suppression weakens substantially between z = 0 and z = 1. For the one point measured, it drops from 13.0% to 7.0% at k = 3 h/Mpc.
- The emulator's k-grid ends at about 12.6 h/Mpc, so the suppression minimum and any high-k upturn are not resolved.
- None of the points sampled reaches the 10 ± 2% suppression at k = 1 h/Mpc reported from eROSITA plus kSZ data. The shortfall is about 2.8 to 3.2 sigma, but this rests on literature values that have not been verified verbatim.
- Two points with very different S(k) have the same gas fraction at M500c ≈ 1.26e14 Msun/h, so the van Daalen-type relation between gas fraction and suppression is not reproduced by the pair tested.

For weak lensing, the evidence is taken from the literature rather than our own forecast:

- An Omega_m bias of -5.7 sigma arises for a Euclid-like survey when Illustris-like feedback is fitted with a one-parameter HMCode model. A theoretical-error covariance removes most of this bias.
- Reconciling DES Y3 with Planck needs A_mod = 0.858 ± 0.052. The suppression this implies at k ≈ 0.2 h/Mpc appears much larger than anything the emulator produces there.

## Background

**Physics of the suppression.** AGN feedback, with stellar feedback in lower-mass haloes, drives gas out of group- and cluster-mass haloes (about 1e13 to 1e14.5 Msun). This lowers their baryon fractions and flattens their inner mass profiles. The result is a suppression of P(k) relative to dark-matter-only runs at k ≈ 0.1–10 h/Mpc. At higher k, cooling and star formation push the ratio back up.

**Link to halo baryon fractions.** Several studies find that the suppression is set mainly by the baryon fraction of group-scale haloes:

- the van Daalen et al. library of 92 simulation power-spectrum ratios (arXiv:1906.00968);
- halo-model work tying observed gas profiles to P(k) (arXiv:1908.05765);
- a BAHAMAS/cosmo-OWLS breakdown by halo mass (arXiv:2309.06479);
- an IllustrisTNG study of which halo masses and radii matter at k > 1 h/Mpc (arXiv:2511.10634);
- the FLAMINGO resummation model, which predicts suppression from observed halo baryon fractions (arXiv:2509.04552).

FLAMINGO also studies the baryon response across feedback variants calibrated to cluster gas fractions (arXiv:2410.17109). This link makes X-ray, tSZ and kSZ observations direct probes of the suppression.

**Public modelling tools.** These include the BACCO baryonification emulator (arXiv:2011.15018), BCemu (arXiv:2108.08863), HMcode-2020 with its log10 T_AGN parameter (arXiv:2009.01858), an analytic redshift-independent formulation (arXiv:2504.15633), and the CAMELS simulation suite (arXiv:2010.00619).

**Observational constraints.**

- Siegel et al. (arXiv:2512.02954) combine eROSITA gas fractions with kSZ profiles and infer 10 ± 2% suppression at k = 1 h/Mpc. This is stronger than fiducial FLAMINGO and BAHAMAS. HSC-XXL gas fractions give 5 ± 4%.
- Grandis et al. (arXiv:2309.02920) infer 0.042 (+0.012/−0.014) at k = 1 h/Mpc and 0.184 (+0.026/−0.031) at k = 3 h/Mpc from cluster gas and stellar fractions. They predict a change of less than 1% for k < 0.37 h/Mpc at 97.5% credibility.

Neither set of numbers has yet been checked against the full text; both come from abstract-level reading.

**Weak lensing.** Ignoring these scale-dependent changes biases S8 (arXiv:1105.1075). Feedback is also degenerate with neutrino mass (arXiv:1407.4301). Amon and Efstathiou (arXiv:2206.11794) and Preston, Amon and Efstathiou (arXiv:2305.09827) model P_m = P_L + A_mod (P_NL − P_L). They argue that stronger-than-standard nonlinear suppression can reconcile cosmic shear with Planck. Further evidence for strong feedback is cited in arXiv:2602.02484.

Mitigation strategies in the literature are:

- scale cuts;
- marginalising over baryonic parameters;
- theoretical-error covariances (arXiv:2410.12500);
- external SZ, kSZ or FRB constraints (arXiv:2301.02186, arXiv:2401.03510, arXiv:2501.17922).

## Results

### Emulator configuration

The Pk-ratio emulator has these properties:

- **Redshifts:** trained at z = 0, 0.1, 0.5, 1.0 and 2.0.
- **k-grid:** 799 bins from 0.022 to about 12.6 h/Mpc. The k units are h/Mpc according to the file headers.
- **Parameter bounds:**

| Parameter | Range |
|---|---|
| kappa_w | 2–4 |
| e_w | 0.2–1.0 |
| M_seed | 0.6–2.0 (units of 1e6 Msun) |
| v_kin | 0.1–1.2 |
| eps_kin | 0.02–1.2 |
| omega_m | 0.12–0.155 |
| sigma_8 | 0.7–0.9 |

- **Reference spectrum:** the ratio is taken relative to P_grav, a gravity-only run. Whether this is equivalent to the P_DMO used in the literature has not been checked.

All parameter points below lie within these bounds. Their full parameter labels, read from the prediction-file headers, are:

| Point | kappa_w | e_w | M_seed | v_kin | eps_kin |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| fiducial | 3 | 0.6 | 1.3 | 0.65 | 0.61 |
| strongAGN | 3 | 1.0 | 1.3 | 1.2 | 1.2 |
| weakAGN | 3 | 0.2 | 1.3 | 0.1 | 0.02 |
| maxsupp | 2 | 1.0 | 2.0 | 1.2 | 1.2 |
| maxsupp_lowkin | 2 | 1.0 | 2.0 | 0.1 | 0.02 |
| maxsupp_lowM | 2 | 1.0 | 0.6 | 1.2 | 1.2 |

Every file header lists omega_m = 0.14 and sigma_8 = 0.8, so the cosmology axes were never varied.

### Pk-ratio at z = 0 for the sampled feedback points

**maxsupp (combined extreme corner).** S(k) at z = 0:

| k (h/Mpc) | S(k) |
|---|---|
| 0.101 | 0.99944 ± 0.00003 |
| 0.510 | 0.9868 ± 0.0008 |
| 1.013 | 0.9638 ± 0.0020 |
| 2.002 | 0.9179 ± 0.0045 |
| 3.007 | 0.8698 ± 0.0065 |
| 3.698 | 0.8400 ± 0.0076 |
| 4.00 | 0.8284 ± 0.0079 |
| 5.00 | 0.7942 ± 0.0089 |
| 6.0 | 0.7680 ± 0.0095 |
| 7.01 | 0.7479 ± 0.0100 |
| 7.84 | 0.7356 |

This is 3.6 ± 0.2% suppression at k = 1 and 13.0 ± 0.7% at k = 3 h/Mpc.

**maxsupp_lowM (M_seed = 0.6).** Lowering the seed mass from 2.0 to 0.6 deepens the suppression:

| k (h/Mpc) | S(k) |
|---|---|
| 0.212 | 0.9967 |
| 0.510 | 0.9835 ± 0.0011 |
| 1.013 | 0.9557 ± 0.0029 |
| 2.002 | 0.9026 ± 0.0064 |
| 3.007 | 0.8521 ± 0.0094 |
| 3.698 | 0.8228 ± 0.0109 |

This is 4.4 ± 0.3% at k = 1 and 14.8 ± 0.9% at k = 3 h/Mpc, the largest suppression among the sampled points. It is not shown to be the maximum over the design range.

**maxsupp_lowkin (kinetic parameters at minimum).** This point shows essentially no suppression:

| k (h/Mpc) | S(k) |
|---|---|
| 0.212 | 1.0002 |
| 0.510 | 1.0004 ± 0.0007 |
| 1.013 | 1.0006 ± 0.0019 |
| 2.002 | 1.0033 ± 0.0042 |
| 3.007 | 0.9972 ± 0.0062 |
| 3.698 | 0.9883 ± 0.0071 |

In this emulator, v_kin and eps_kin therefore drive almost all the suppression up to k ≈ 3.7 h/Mpc, even with e_w at its maximum.

**fiducial versus strongAGN.** The S(k) values are:

| Point | k = 1.01 | k = 3.01 | k = 3.70 |
|---|---|---|---|
| fiducial | 0.9779 | 0.9197 | 0.8984 (std 0.004) |
| strongAGN | 0.9746 | 0.9121 | 0.8909 |

Raising the kinetic parameters and e_w at kappa_w = 3 therefore adds only about 0.3–0.8 percentage points of suppression over this range. These values come from an earlier run on this thread and were not independently re-verified in the present run.

**strongAGN beyond k = 3.7 h/Mpc.** S(k) continues to fall:

| k (h/Mpc) | S(k) |
|---|---|
| 5.25 | 0.851 |
| 7.01 | 0.8205 |
| 10.01 | 0.7946 (std 0.0098) |
| 12.55 | 0.7893 |

Between about 11.6 and 12.6 h/Mpc it flattens to a plateau of about 0.789–0.790, falling by less than 0.001 per 0.1 h/Mpc at the edge.

Two cautions apply to the high-k behaviour:

- The ratio has no upturn within the grid. The minimum is at or beyond k_max ≈ 12.6 h/Mpc, with a depth of about 21% for strongAGN.
- maxsupp is already at 0.7356 by k = 7.84, deeper than the strongAGN plateau. Its minimum is unresolved.

The k_max and plateau values come from byte offsets, and the final rows of the file were not quoted verbatim. They should be treated as approximate.

### Redshift evolution, z = 0 to z = 1

For maxsupp the suppression weakens strongly towards z = 1:

| k (h/Mpc) | S at z = 0 | S at z = 1 | Suppression, z = 0 to z = 1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1.013 | 0.9638 ± 0.0020 | 0.9781 ± 0.0018 | 3.6% to 2.2% |
| 3.007 | 0.8698 ± 0.0065 | 0.9299 ± 0.0055 | 13.0% to 7.0% |
| 3.70 | 0.8400 ± 0.0076 | 0.9214 ± 0.0064 | 16.0% to 7.9% |

Qualitatively, this matches the FLAMINGO statement that the response grows as z falls (arXiv:2410.17109). That comparison has not been checked against the FLAMINGO text. The ratio is still falling at k = 3.7 at both redshifts, so any shift of the minimum with redshift could not be measured.

[[FIGURE 28]]

Figure 28 plots the emulator Pk-ratio at z = 0 and z = 1 for the fiducial and maxsupp points. Only the maxsupp values in the table above were read out numerically. The fiducial z = 1 prediction was written but not read, so no quantitative z-trend is claimed for the fiducial point.

A planned companion plot of the four z = 0 variants was overwritten by this one, because the two plotting calls shared an output path.

### Gas fraction versus suppression

The fGas emulator gives M_gas/M500c inside R500c at z = 0 in three M500c bins: 5.01e13, 7.94e13 and 1.26e14 Msun/h.

| Point | f_gas at 1.26e14 Msun/h | f_gas at 7.94e13 Msun/h |
|---|---|---|
| fiducial | 0.1214 ± 0.0010 | 0.1090 |
| strongAGN | 0.1221 ± 0.0019 | 0.1098 |
| weakAGN | 0.1414 ± 0.0023 | 0.1375 |

Only fiducial and strongAGN have S(k) values to pair with these gas fractions. Their f_gas values agree within errors, with strongAGN nominally higher, yet strongAGN is 0.3–0.8 points more suppressed. This pair therefore shows no resolvable van Daalen-type relation (arXiv:1906.00968), and the nominal trend runs the wrong way.

The comparison has two weaknesses:

- It is confounded, because e_w changes together with the kinetic parameters.
- It is limited, because the weakAGN S(k) was never read. weakAGN has a markedly higher gas fraction, so it is the point that would make a three-point test meaningful.

One physical reading of the pair is that the emulator's suppression is driven by gas removed beyond R500c, or by haloes of other masses, rather than by the R500c gas fraction. This is untested.

### Comparison with observational suppression estimates

Errors are combined in quadrature, taking the published error on the side facing the emulator value. For maxsupp:

| Constraint | Gap |
|---|---|
| Grandis et al., k = 1 | 0.4 sigma (4.2% vs 3.6%) |
| Grandis et al., k = 3 | 1.7 sigma (18.4% vs 13.0%) |
| eROSITA + kSZ, k = 1 | 3.2 sigma short (10% vs 3.6%) |
| HSC-XXL, k = 1 | 0.35 sigma |

An earlier pass quoted about 3 and 8 sigma against Grandis et al. Those figures used emulator error alone and are superseded.

The strongest point, maxsupp_lowM, is:

- about 2.8 sigma short of eROSITA + kSZ;
- consistent with HSC-XXL and with Grandis et al. at k = 1;
- 3.6 points below Grandis et al. at k = 3.

All of these significances depend on literature values that have not been confirmed verbatim. They are also tested only at the kappa_w = 2, e_w = 1 corners with fixed cosmology.

### Weak-lensing impact (literature-based)

**Omega_m bias from ignoring or mis-modelling baryons.** Maraio, Hall and Taylor (arXiv:2410.12500, Table 3, read verbatim) consider an idealised Euclid-like Stage-IV cosmic-shear survey with ell_max = 5000:

| Ground truth | Model | 100 ΔΩ_m | Significance |
|---|---|---|---|
| Illustris | one-parameter HMCode, no theory error | −1.317 | −5.69 sigma |
| Illustris | same, with theoretical-error covariance | 0.128 | 0.249 sigma |
| Bahamas | one-parameter HMCode | 0.057 | 0.258 sigma |
| Eagle | six-parameter model, with theory error | 0.573 | 1.459 sigma |

The text adds two statements:

- The one-parameter model without theory error gives "at least a 3 sigma offset in either Omega_m or S8 for all hydro-sims excluding Bahamas".
- With Simba as ground truth, even ell_max = 1000 is biased by more than 2 sigma in all parameters.

The ΔS8 values are in that paper's Table 4, which was not read. This bias is therefore an Omega_m bias, not an S8 bias.

**Suppression needed to reconcile lensing with Planck.**

- For DES Y3, A_mod = 0.858 ± 0.052, with no scale cuts and a Planck prior (arXiv:2305.09827, Eq. 3). The suppression must extend to k ~ 0.2 h/Mpc.
- For KiDS-1000, A_mod ≈ 0.69 (arXiv:2206.11794).
- Without A_mod, DES Y3 S8 lies 0.9–1.8 sigma below Planck S8 = 0.828 ± 0.016, depending on analysis variant.

**Comparison with the emulator.** For maxsupp, S(k) is 0.9994 at k = 0.10 and 0.987 at k = 0.51 h/Mpc. The value at k ≈ 0.2 h/Mpc was not read but presumably lies below a 1% effect. For maxsupp_lowM the read value at k = 0.212 is 0.9967.

Emulator-level feedback therefore agrees with the Grandis et al. bound of less than 1% for k < 0.37 h/Mpc. It appears far weaker than A_mod = 0.86 or 0.69 would require at these scales. This is a qualitative comparison, because no A_mod-equivalent number was computed for any emulator point.

### Bibliographic and data products

Validated citation entries for arXiv:2305.09827, arXiv:2410.12500, arXiv:2512.02954 and arXiv:2309.02920, each with a verbatim abstract quote, were written to `runs/261023_143127/references.bib`.

Full texts of FLAMINGO (arXiv:2410.17109), Siegel et al. (arXiv:2512.02954) and Grandis et al. (arXiv:2309.02920) were downloaded to `runs/261023_143127/` as `.txt` files. They have not yet been read.

## Discussion

**Feedback physics in the emulator.** Within this emulator, the kinetic AGN mode is the lever on S(k). Switching it off removes almost all suppression even at maximum e_w. Lowering the seed mass, and plausibly lowering kappa_w (not isolated, because M_seed also changed), deepens it.

This is consistent with the general picture of AGN-driven gas expulsion from group-scale haloes. However, the emulator does not show the expected anti-correlation between the gas fraction inside R500c at about 1e14 Msun/h and the suppression. Possible reasons:

- the relevant gas is pushed beyond R500c;
- other halo masses dominate;
- the two-point comparison is simply too confounded to show it.

The literature (arXiv:1906.00968, arXiv:2509.04552, arXiv:2309.06479) predicts a clear relation, so this is a real tension worth resolving with the unread weakAGN curve and single-parameter sweeps.

**Size of the suppression.** The emulator's largest sampled suppression at k = 1 h/Mpc, 4.4%, agrees with HSC-XXL and Grandis et al. It falls short of the strong-feedback eROSITA + kSZ inference. At k = 3 h/Mpc it is below Grandis et al.

Three explanations are open:

- the design range may not span the strongest feedback now favoured observationally;
- the cosmology axes, untouched here, may shift the response through the baryon fraction and halo abundance;
- the P_grav reference may differ from P_DMO.

- The text says the one-parameter model without theory error gives at least a 3 sigma offset in either Omega_m or S8 for every hydro simulation except Bahamas. For Simba as ground truth, even ell_max = 1000 is biased by more than 2 sigma in all parameters.

2. HACC maxsupp z=0 Pk-ratio beyond k=3.7 h/Mpc (f-032; tc-...-83). Values are 0.8284 at k=4.0, 0.7942 at k=5.0, 0.7680 at k=6.0, 0.7479 at k=7.0 and 0.7356 at k=7.84 h/Mpc. This is already deeper than the strongAGN plateau of about 0.789 (f-017).

3. HACC suppression versus the A_mod requirement: this comparison is qualitative only, since the k=0.2-0.3 values are unread.
- From f-024, S(k) goes from 0.9994 at k=0.10 to 0.987 at k=0.51 h/Mpc, so at k~0.2 it is presumably below 1%.

brief.summary: Note first: I have no hydrodynamics or baryonic emulator tool. My only tools were arXiv and web search, so I did not compute any z=0 Pk-ratio (P_hydro/P_DMO) values. Any numbers for specific parameter points have to come from running BACCO (2011.15018), BCemu (2108.08863), HMcode-2020 (2009.01858) or the van Daalen et al. power-spectrum library (1906.00968) locally. I give no suppression amplitudes because I did not read results beyond titles and short abstracts. Physics: AGN feedback, and stellar feedback in lower-mass haloes, pushes gas out of group- and cluster-mass haloes (about 1e13-1e14.5 Msun). This lowers their baryon fraction and flattens their inner mass profiles, which suppresses P(k) at k of about 0.1-10 h/Mpc relative to dark-matter-only runs. At higher k, gas cooling and star formation push the ratio back up. Several groups (van Daalen 1906.00968, resummation model 2509.04552, Debackere 1908.05765, BAHAMAS/cosmo-OWLS 2309.06479, TNG 2511.10634) find the suppression is mainly set by the baryon fraction of group-scale haloes. That ties it to X-ray, tSZ and kSZ observables. For weak lensing, these scale-dependent changes bias S8 if left out (1105.1075, 1407.4301). Amon and Efstathiou (2206.11794, 2305.09827) argue that stronger-than-standard nonlinear suppression could reconcile KiDS and DES cosmic shear with Planck, and recent kSZ/X-ray results (FLAMINGO 2410.17109, 2602.02484) hint that feedback may be stronger than in fiducial simulations. Current mitigation options are scale cuts, marginalising over HMcode or baryonification parameters, theory-error covariances (2410.12500), and outside constraints from SZ, X-ray or FRBs (2301.02186, 2401.03510, 2501.17922).

result.summary:
I ran three HACC Pk-ratio (P_hydro/P_grav) predictions at z=0 with cosmology held fixed (omega_m=0.14, sigma_8=0.8, kappa_w=3, M_seed=1.3). Two success criteria are not fully met: values at k=5-10 h/Mpc and the location and depth of the suppression minimum were not extracted. The text reader cuts each 799-bin CSV off near k=3.7 h/Mpc, and load_table_data rejects the CSV header row (posted as q-06). The fiducial point is the centre of the parameter ranges, not a calibrated fiducial.

Parameter points:
- fiducial_z0: e_w=0.6, v_kin=0.65, eps_kin=0.61
- strongAGN_z0: e_w=1.0, v_kin=1.2, eps_kin=1.2
- weakAGN_z0: e_w=0.2, v_kin=0.1, eps_kin=0.02

Ratio at k=0.10 / 0.51 / 1.00 / 2.00 / 3.0 / 3.71 h/Mpc:
- Fiducial: 0.99968 / 0.99197 / 0.97832+/-0.00096 / 0.95104+/-0.00229 / 0.91968 / 0.8979
- Strong: 0.99962 / 0.99062 / 0.97506+/-0.00175 / 0.94463+/-0.00405 / 0.91207 / 0.8904
- Weak: 1.00009 / 1.00096 / 1.0023+/-0.0025 / 1.0089 / 1.0074 / 1.0012+/-0.0105. This is an enhancement, peaking at about 1.0097 near k=2.4 h/Mpc.

For the fiducial and strong points the suppression is still deepening at k=3.7 h/Mpc, so their minimum lies above k=3.7 h/Mpc.

Comparison at k=1 h/Mpc: suppression is 2.2% (fiducial), 2.5% (strong) and -0.2% (weak). All three agree with HSC-XXL (5+/-4%) within about 1.4 sigma. None reaches eROSITA+kSZ (10+/-2%, 2512.02954); the strong point falls short by about 3.7 sigma. Pushing e_w, v_kin and eps_kin together to their upper limits changes the k=1 suppression by only about 0.3 percentage points relative to the fiducial. The emulator 1-sigma at k=1 (0.1-0.25%) is comparable to that fiducial-to-strong difference but well below the weak-to-fiducial difference (2.4%).

result.summary:
This direction is only partly done. The literature synthesis is posted as finding f-003 and rests on the abstracts and introductions of five full texts. These are saved under /Users/nramachandra/hep-genesis-testing/projects/ramp-combo-baryonic-pk/runs/261017_143153/ as 2410.17109.txt, 2512.02954.txt, 2309.07959.txt, 2206.11794.txt and 2309.02920.txt.

Mechanism, from those texts:
- Energy injected by AGN moves gas relative to the dark matter and suppresses small-scale power by tens of percent compared with dark-matter-only runs (2512.02954).
- Below about 10 Mpc, AGN push baryons outward, while on smaller scales star formation concentrates baryons in halo centres (2309.02920).
- In FLAMINGO (2410.17109), the response is stronger for lower group and cluster gas fractions, for collimated jets instead of thermal winds, and for lower stellar mass at fixed gas fraction.
- As redshift falls, the FLAMINGO response grows and its minimum moves to smaller scales. The dependence on cosmology is about 1 percent at k<10 h/Mpc. Its emulator is accurate to better than 1 percent up to k=10 h/Mpc and z=3.

Benchmarks at k=1 h/Mpc:
- eROSITA plus kSZ: 10 +/- 2 percent; HSC-XXL: 5 +/- 4 percent. Both are for haloes with 13<log10 M500<14 at 0<z<1 (2512.02954).
- Cluster-based baryon-correction priors (2309.02920): 0.042 (+0.012/-0.014) at k=1 h/Mpc and 0.184 (+0.026/-0.031) at k=3 h/Mpc. The effect is below 1 percent for k<0.37 h/Mpc at 97.5 percent credibility.

Weak lensing:

result.summary:
Three papers were read and cited with verbatim quotes in /Users/nramachandra/hep-genesis-testing/projects/ramp-combo-baryonic-pk/runs/261017_143153/references.bib.

(1) Amon & Efstathiou (2206.11794): KiDS-1000 cosmic shear is consistent with Planck LCDM if non-linear power is suppressed with A_mod ~ 0.69. The suppression must extend to k ~ 0.2 h/Mpc, which is well outside the BAHAMAS range.

(2) FLAMINGO (2309.07959): across its range of feedback variants, baryonic effects are not large enough to remove the S8 tension; the paper says 'it is unlikely that baryon physics is driving this modification'.

(3) Siegel et al. (2512.02954): joint eROSITA and kSZ data give 10+/-2% suppression at k=1 h/Mpc, while HSC-XXL gives 5+/-4%. Only the strong-feedback runs BAHAMAS 8.0 and FLAMINGO fgas-8sigma agree with the eROSITA and kSZ result, and the simulations differ from each other by more than 10% at k=1 h/Mpc. Mitigation, from their LSST Y1-like mock (Fig. 6 of that paper): with no baryon model, S8 is significantly biased. An uninformed baryonification model removes the bias but halves the precision. A prior calibrated on kSZ and eROSITA recovers half of the lost precision. The paper reports this bias only graphically and gives no numerical S8 shift.

Findings f-004 (the literature numbers) and f-005 (qualitative comparison framework) are posted. The comparison with d-01 is only a framework so far, because the d-01 emulator values at k=1 h/Mpc were not on the board when I posted. Only part of this direction got done. I have one numerical cosmology bias from ignoring baryons, but it is an Omega_m bias, not an S8 bias, and I did not read the HACC values at k=0.2-0.3 h/Mpc.

What was established:

1. Omega_m bias from Maraio, Hall and Taylor (arXiv:2410.12500, Table 3), read verbatim (f-031; tc-...-86). Survey configuration: an idealised Euclid-like Stage-IV cosmic-shear survey with ell_max = 5000.
- Illustris as ground truth, analysed with the one-parameter HMCode model and no theory error: 100*Delta Omega_m = -1.317, which is -5.69 sigma.
- The same case with the theoretical-error covariance added: 0.128, or 0.249 sigma.
- Bahamas as ground truth with the one-parameter model: 0.057, or 0.258 sigma.
- Eagle with the six-parameter model and the theory error included: still 0.573, or 1.459 sigma.
- The text says the one-parameter model without theory error gives at least a 3 sigma offset in either Omega_m or S8 for every hydro simulation except Bahamas. For Simba as ground truth, even ell_max = 1000 is biased by more than 2 sigma in all parameters.
- The full text is saved at runs/261023_143127/2410.12500.txt. The Delta S8 values are in Table 4, past character 55000 of that file, and I did not read them.

2. HACC maxsupp z=0 Pk-ratio beyond k=3.7 h/Mpc (f-032; tc-...-83). Values are 0.8284 at k=4.0, 0.7942 at k=5.0, 0.7680 at k=6.0, 0.7479 at k=7.0 and 0.7356 at k=7.84 h/Mpc. This is already deeper than the strongAGN plateau of about 0.789 (f-017).
- Source file: runs/261023_143127/maxsupp_z0/Pk-ratio_z0.0000_prediction.csv.

3. HACC suppression versus the A_mod requirement: this comparison is qualitative only, since the k=0.2-0.3 values are unread.
- From f-024, S(k) goes from 0.9994 at k=0.10 to 0.987 at k=0.51 h/Mpc, so at k~0.2 it is presumably below 1%.
- That is consistent with Grandis et al.'s bound of less than 1% for k < 0.37 h/Mpc.
- It is far weaker than the suppression that A_mod = 0.858+/-0.052 (DES Y3) or about 0.69 (KiDS-1000) would need at k~0.2 h/Mpc.
- On this basis, HACC-level feedback is unlikely to resolve S8. That conclusion rests on interpolation, not on read-out values.

findings.claim: Literature synthesis from full texts that were read: (1) Mechanism: energy from active galactic nuclei (AGN) moves gas relative to the dark matter. This suppresses the nonlinear matter power by tens of percent compared with dark-matter-only runs (2512.02954). Below about 10 Mpc, AGN redistribute baryons outward, while on smaller scales star formation concentrates baryons in halo centres (2309.02920). In FLAMINGO, lower group and cluster gas fractions, collimated jets instead of thermal winds, and lower stellar mass at fixed gas fraction all strengthen the response. As z falls, the response grows and its minimum moves to smaller scales. The cosmology dependence is about 1 percent at k<10 h/Mpc (2410.17109). (2) Benchmarks: suppression at k=1 h/Mpc is 10+/-2 percent from eROSITA plus kSZ and 5+/-4 percent from HSC-XXL, over 13<log10 M500/(Msun/h)<14 and 0<z<1 (2512.02954). Cluster baryon-correction-model priors give 0.042 (+0.012/-0.014) at k=1 h/Mpc and 0.184 (+0.026/-0.031) at k=3 h/Mpc, with less than 1 percent impact at k<0.37 h/Mpc at 97.5 percent credibility (2309.02920). (3) Weak lensing: Amon and Efstathiou find that KiDS-1000 (S8 = 0.759 +0.024/-0.021) can be reconciled with Planck LCDM if nonlinear power is suppressed more strongly than simulations predict (2206.11794). FLAMINGO finds baryonic effects are not large enough to remove the S8 tension (2309.07959). Mitigation is to calibrate feedback with multi-wavelength gas observables (2512.02954).

findings.claim: Preston, Amon & Efstathiou (2305.09827) find that to reconcile DES Y3 cosmic shear with Planck LCDM, the non-linear suppression needed is weaker than the KiDS-1000 value (A_mod ~ 0.69). It is still more extreme than recent hydrodynamic simulations predict, and it must extend into the mildly non-linear regime, to k ~ 0.2 h/Mpc. findings.claim: Second mitigation method (Maraio, Hall & Taylor, 2410.12500): a theoretical-error covariance built into the matter power spectrum, used in place of binary ell scale cuts. For a Euclid-like survey with ell_max = 5000, even multi-parameter baryon models can introduce significant bias. The theoretical error reduces the bias in Omega_m and S8 to acceptable levels with only a modest increase in variance, and it removes the need to choose an ell_max for each bin. This places the baryon-sensitive shear range up to ell ~ 5000.

findings.claim: Approximate comparison only. The HACC emulator gives about 0.8-0.9% suppression at k=0.5 h/Mpc, about 0.03-0.04% at k=0.1 h/Mpc and at most 2.5% at k=1 h/Mpc (f-001, f-002). This is far below the A_mod-type suppression that Amon-Efstathiou and Preston et al. require. That suppression scales the whole non-linear part of P(k) (A_mod ~ 0.69 for KiDS, weaker but still beyond simulations for DES) and reaches down to k ~ 0.2 h/Mpc. Within its design range, the emulator cannot approach the suppression needed to reconcile shear with Planck. A projected C_ell or xi_+ forecast is future work, since no tool computes it.

Their second model gives 0.049 (+0.016/-0.012) and 0.179 (+0.018/-0.020). At 97.5 percent credibility the impact is below 1% for k<0.37 h/Mpc. findings.claim: Grandis et al. (arXiv:2309.02920) use cluster gas and stellar fractions to infer a suppression of 0.042 (+0.012/-0.014) at k = 1 h/Mpc and 0.184 (+0.026/-0.031) at k = 3 h/Mpc. They predict, at 97.5% credibility, that baryons change P(k) by less than 1% for k < 0.37 h/Mpc, and on that basis question whether baryon feedback drives the cosmic-shear vs CMB S8 discrepancy.

Preston, Amon and Efstathiou (arXiv:2305.09827) model P_m = P_L + A_mod (P_NL - P_L). Their KiDS-1000 Paper I value is A_mod ≈ 0.69. For DES Y3 the abstract says only that the required suppression is "not as strong as inferred using KiDS data, but is still more extreme than predictions from recent numerical simulations", and that it must extend to k ~ 0.2 h/Mpc. The DES Y3 numerical A_mod was not in the portion of the text read so far.

Maraio, Hall and Taylor (arXiv:2410.12500) find that for a Euclid-like survey with ell_max = 5000, even multi-parameter baryon models (including HMCode-2020) can bias Omega_m and S8 significantly. A theoretical-error covariance on P(k) reduces this bias to acceptable levels with only a modest increase in parameter variances. The abstract gives no numerical S8 shift.

At z=0 the combined extreme HACC point (kappa_w=2, e_w=1.0, M_seed=2.0, v_kin=1.2, eps_kin=1.2, omega_m=0.14, sigma_8=0.8) gives P_hydro/P_grav = 0.99944+/-0.00003 at k=0.101, 0.9868+/-0.0008 at k=0.510, 0.9638+/-0.0020 at k=1.013, 0.9179+/-0.0045 at k=2.002, 0.8698+/-0.0065 at k=3.007 and 0.8400+/-0.0076 at k=3.698 h/Mpc. That is a suppression of 3.6+/-0.2% at k=1 and 13.0+/-0.7% at k=3. Against HSC-XXL (5+/-4% at k=1) the gap is 0.35 sigma, so the point is consistent. Against eROSITA+kSZ (10+/-2% at k=1) it falls short by 3.2 sigma. Against 2309.02920 (4.2% at k=1, 18.4% at k=3) it is 0.6 points low at k=1 (about 3 sigma of emulator error alone) and 5.4 points low at k=3 (about 8 sigma of emulator error alone). This point reaches neither 10% at k=1 nor 18% at k=3.

The HACC fGas emulator at z=0 has 3 M500c bins: 5.01e13, 7.94e13 and 1.26e14 Msun/h. In the bin nearest 1e14 (1.26e14 Msun/h), f_gas = 0.1214+/-0.0010 for fiducial, 0.1221+/-0.0019 for strongAGN and 0.1414+/-0.0023 for weakAGN (e_w=0.2, v_kin=0.1, eps_kin=0.02). At 7.94e13 Msun/h the values are 0.1090, 0.1098 and 0.1375.

Partial answer to q-12. Only two fGas points have S(k) read so far. Fiducial: f_gas(1.26e14) = 0.1214+/-0.0010, with S(k=1) = 0.9779 and S(k=3) = 0.9197. StrongAGN: f_gas = 0.1221+/-0.0019, with S(k=1) = 0.9746 and S(k=3) = 0.9121. The two f_gas values agree within errors; strongAGN is nominally higher, yet its suppression is 0.3-0.8 points deeper. Between these two points there is therefore no resolvable van Daalen-type relation, and the nominal trend runs the wrong way. WeakAGN has a much higher f_gas (0.1414), but its S(k) was not read in this direction, so a three-point test is still open. The strongAGN vs fiducial comparison is confounded: e_w changes (0.6 to 1.0) at the same time as v_kin and eps_kin.

The HACC maxsupp_lowkin point at z=0 (kappa_w=2, e_w=1.0, M_seed=2.0, v_kin=0.1, eps_kin=0.02, omega_m=0.14, sigma_8=0.8) shows essentially no suppression. P_hydro/P_grav is 1.0002 at k=0.212, 1.0004+/-0.0007 at k=0.510, 1.0006+/-0.0019 at k=1.013, 1.0033+/-0.0042 at k=2.002, 0.9972+/-0.0062 at k=3.007 and 0.9883+/-0.0071 at k=3.698 h/Mpc. So in this emulator the kinetic AGN parameters (v_kin, eps_kin) drive almost all of the suppression at k up to 3.7 h/Mpc, even with e_w at its maximum.

The HACC maxsupp_lowM point at z=0 (kappa_w=2, e_w=1.0, M_seed=0.6, v_kin=1.2, eps_kin=1.2, omega_m=0.14, sigma_8=0.8) suppresses more than the combined maxsupp point (M_seed=2.0). P_hydro/P_grav is 0.9967 at k=0.212, 0.9835+/-0.0011 at k=0.510, 0.9557+/-0.0029 at k=1.013, 0.9026+/-0.0064 at k=2.002, 0.8521+/-0.0094 at k=3.007 and 0.8228+/-0.0109 at k=3.698 h/Mpc. The maxsupp values are 0.9638, 0.8698 and 0.8400 at k=1, 3 and 3.7. The suppression is 4.4+/-0.3% at k=1 and 14.8+/-0.9% at k=3, so maxsupp is not the strongest point, and low M_seed increases the suppression. This is still short of eROSITA+kSZ (10+/-2% at k=1, arXiv:2512.02954) by about 2.8 sigma. It is consistent with HSC-XXL (5+/-4%) and with Grandis et al. at k=1 (4.2%). At k=3 it is 3.6 points below Grandis (18.4%). Among the points read, the HACC design range does not reach the eROSITA+kSZ level at k=1.

The S8 impact will come from the literature rather than our own shear forecast, because no tool computes C_ell or xi_plus. Should a projected-lensing estimate be flagged as future work?
Are the emulator's uncertainties at z=0 small compared with the differences between feedback variants, so that the conclusions are meaningful?

Over budget. Five or six papers, each needing download_arxiv_full_text, several read_arxiv_chunk calls and cite, plus get_paper_figures, comes to well over 20 calls. Narrow d-02 to the AGN feedback physics: 2410.17109 (full text, one figure), 2309.02920 or 2309.06479 for halo mass and baryon fraction, and 1104.1174 for the 10-30 percent minimum at 5-20 h/Mpc and the high-k upturn, which the brief flagged as unsourced general knowledge. Three (fGas, suppression) pairs give a monotonicity check, not a fitted relation. State this explicitly. Report fGas at a stated halo mass bin near 1e14 Msun, taken from the tool output.

contested.reason: The claim that the k=1 h/Mpc suppression 'across the full design range of the AGN and kinetic parameters' spans only about -0.2% to +2.5% is not supported. Only three corner-like points were run. kappa_w (fixed at 3), M_seed and cosmology were never varied, and the parameter bounds were not shown in any cited evidence (no describe_parameters output). The quoted CSV excerpts (tc-...-49, -31, -37) also stop at k=0.117 h/Mpc. The peak of 1.0097 near k=2.4 and the k=1 and k=3.71 values are not visible in the evidence; only the k=0.101 value (1.00009) can be checked. The weak-point measurements may be right, but the design-range generalisation must be removed or backed by a parameter scan.

Every evidence excerpt is the title and author header (chars 0-4000) of a paper. None contains the specific numbers claimed: 10+/-2 and 5+/-4 percent, 0.042 and 0.184 at k=1 and 3 h/Mpc, k<0.37 at 97.5 percent, S8=0.759, or about 1 percent cosmology dependence. 2309.02920 was never cited through the cite tool, so no verbatim quote is stored for its numbers. The numbers are plausible and partly corroborated by f-004 for 2512.02954, but this finding's own evidence does not contain them.

issues.text: The quoted CSV excerpts stop at k=0.117 h/Mpc. The values at k=0.51, 1, 2, 3 and 3.71 are not visible in the cited evidence; only the k=0.101 values (0.99968 fiducial, 0.99962 strong) can be checked. The k=1 values are the key numbers of the task and should be re-extracted with a working reader and quoted directly (q-06). The finding is accepted on the summary's account, but this is a weak point.

Wording of the comparison. The phrase 'eROSITA+kSZ ... excluded at more than 3.5 sigma' reverses the logic. The emulator cannot exclude a measurement. The correct statement is that the sampled HACC points fall short of the eROSITA+kSZ value by about 3.7 sigma (observational error only). The comparison also mixes a fixed HACC cosmology (omega_m=0.14, probably omega_m h^2) with observational constraints derived under a different cosmology and halo-mass weighting. It should be framed as a range-of-model check, as critique c-01 required.

There is a physics discrepancy no one has noted. At k=3 h/Mpc the HACC fiducial and strong points give about 8-9 percent suppression, while the cluster-calibrated prior of 2309.02920 gives 18.4 percent (+2.6/-3.1). At k=1 the emulator gives 2.2-2.5 percent against 4.2 percent there and 5-10 percent from 2512.02954. In addition, the weak-AGN point shows a net enhancement, and the strong AGN parameters barely matter (0.3 percentage points). Together these suggest that the parameters held fixed (kappa_w, M_seed), or the parameter interpretation itself, control most of the suppression. This must be resolved before any conclusion about feedback strength.

Two sourcing gaps remain (q-05). 2309.02920 has no stored citation or quote. The depth and k of FLAMINGO's z=0 minimum, which the brief listed as a quantity to check, is still unsourced, and so are the 1104.1174 claims of a 10-30 percent minimum at 5-20 h/Mpc and the high-k upturn.

'Consistent with Planck LCDM only if' is stronger than the source. Amon and Efstathiou show that suppression with A_mod about 0.69 is sufficient, not that it is the only route. 'Costs 2x in precision' should be stated precisely: the S8 uncertainty roughly doubles.
f-005 was written before the d-01 numbers were available and is now stale. It should be replaced by an explicit comparison table: HACC at k=1 and k=3 versus 2309.02920, HSC-XXL and eROSITA+kSZ.

No weak-lensing quantity has been estimated. The task asks for the impact on weak-lensing cosmology. A rough projected estimate (which ell range is affected, and the order of magnitude of the xi_+ or C_ell suppression) can be sourced from 1910.11357 or 2305.09827, or derived approximately from the emulator curve. Either must be clearly labelled as such.
